routines.name: Morning Executive Brief
routines.prompt:
Generate the morning executive brief and send it to Slack.

1. Check Gmail for all unread emails since yesterday 5pm:
   - Count total unread
   - Identify urgent items using the urgency framework from your knowledge base
   - Summarize the top 10 most important emails (who, subject, what they need)
   - Draft replies for any that you can handle

2. Check today's Google Calendar:
   - List all meetings with times, attendees, and any prep needed
   - Flag any conflicts or back-to-back meetings without buffers
   - Note any meetings that need prep materials from Drive

3. Check memory for any pending action items or follow-ups due today

4. Send the brief to Slack in this format:
   ---
   MORNING BRIEF — [date]

   URGENT (needs attention now):
   • [items, if any — or "Nothing urgent"]

   TODAY'S CALENDAR:
   • [time] — [meeting] with [people] | [prep needed]

   EMAIL SUMMARY ([count] unread):
   • [sender]: [subject] — [what they need]

   ACTION ITEMS DUE TODAY:
   • [items from tracking sheet]

   DRAFTED REPLIES (ready for your approval):
   • Re: [subject] — [summary of draft]
   ---

5. Save what you reported to memory so you don't re-notify about the same items.

routines.name: Midday Email Check
routines.prompt:
Quick midday email triage — check Gmail for new emails since 7am.

Only alert on Slack if there's something urgent per the urgency framework.
For urgent items, send a brief Slack message:
"URGENT: [who] — [what] — [action needed]"

For non-urgent items, save a summary to memory for the afternoon brief.
Check memory first to avoid re-notifying about items already covered in the morning brief.

routines.name: Pre-Meeting Prep
routines.prompt:
Check Google Calendar for any meetings starting in the next 30 minutes.

If there's a meeting coming up:
1. Look up the attendees (check memory and recent emails for context)
2. Search Google Drive for any relevant docs, decks, or shared files
3. Check if there are related email threads that provide context
4. Send a Slack message 15 minutes before:
   "Meeting in 15 min: [title] with [people]
   Context: [1-2 sentence summary]
   Docs: [links if any]
   Last interaction: [brief note from memory/email]"

If no meetings coming up, do nothing. Don't send "no meetings" messages.
Check memory to avoid sending duplicate prep for the same meeting.

routines.name: Afternoon Recap
routines.prompt:
Generate the afternoon recap and send to Slack.

1. Check Gmail for emails received since the midday check (12pm)
2. Review today's completed meetings — note any action items mentioned
3. Check memory for items noted during the day but not yet reported
4. Update the action items Google Sheet with any new items from today

Send to Slack:
---
AFTERNOON RECAP — [date]

NEW SINCE MORNING:
• [new emails/items that need attention]

TODAY'S ACTION ITEMS (new):
• [items captured from meetings and emails today]

PENDING RESPONSES:
• [emails still awaiting reply, with age]

TOMORROW PREVIEW:
• [first 3 meetings from tomorrow's calendar]
---

Save the recap to memory so tomorrow's morning brief can reference it.

routines.name: Weekly Calendar Review
routines.prompt:
Sunday evening — prepare the week ahead overview.

1. Pull next week's Google Calendar (Monday through Friday)
2. Identify potential conflicts, overloaded days, or missing buffers
3. Check for any meetings that need prep materials
4. Review the action items sheet for overdue items
5. Check LinkedIn and X for any pending messages or mentions from the past week

Send to Slack:
---
WEEK AHEAD — [date range]

MEETING LOAD:
• Mon: [count] meetings ([hours] total)
• Tue: [count] meetings ([hours] total)
• Wed: [count] meetings ([hours] total)
• Thu: [count] meetings ([hours] total)
• Fri: [count] meetings ([hours] total)

HEADS UP:
• [conflicts, heavy days, prep needed]

OVERDUE ACTION ITEMS:
• [items past due date]

SOCIAL UPDATES:
• LinkedIn: [pending messages/mentions]
• X: [pending mentions/DMs]
---
